newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by silver.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Friday, led again by silver, as the recent strong rallies in the dollar and stock market corrected for the second day in a row.

"We've seen a break upwards in silver, with the volatilities picking up, and physical silver could be cheap for fabricators now relative to six months out," said Scott Meyers, senior analyst at Pioneer Futures in New York.
"But the close was weak in both silver and gold and the fundamentals for gold are still nothing to jump for joy about," he said.

COMEX March silver ended up 10.2 cents at $4.977 an ounce after posting a session high of $5.000, the highest level for the contract since late November. Estimated total volume in silver futures was 30,000 contracts.
In the bullion market, silver fixed in London Friday morning at $4.9725, the highest since October 1996.
"Silver has much better fundamentals than gold, but we still have to clear the $5.00 level and I'm not sure that gold is out of the woods yet at all," FIMAT New York trader, John Tyree, said.
COMEX February gold ended up $0.90 at $353.40, below its intraday peak of $355.30. Estimated total volume in gold futures was 48,000 lots, down from Thursday's official tally of 75,282 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $352.30/80 against the London afternoon fix of $352.50 and yesterday's New York close of $351.25/75.
Thursday, spot gold fixed at a new 40-month low of $348.00.
Silver has refused to follow gold lower since the start of 1997, and the spot gold/silver ratio has fallen sharply in the past three weeks to a 10 month low at 70.88 at the close Friday.

Spread trades between gold and silver had contributed to the partial recovery by silver since Thursday, but the move was sparked by fund buying and stop order execution above a three-week-old resistance level at $4.80 in COMEX March silver, analysts said.
In data released Friday, open interest in COMEX silver futures was little changed Thursday.

But gold open interest dropped further, suggesting fund short covering was occurring in gold, as the US dollar's rally lost some momentum and the US stock market saw a second day of sharp falls, analysts said.
Total COMEX gold open interest fell 1,163 lots Thursday to 200,720 contracts, after a fall of 3,588 lots Wednesday.
But some short positions were being rolled into forward months also, with February gold open interest down a further 3,440 lots Thursday and April gold open interest up 1,564 lots.
Gold's fundamentals remained little changed though, analysts said.
Producer hedging was said to be waiting just above current market levels and central bank sales of gold are expected to rise further in 1997, analysts said.
"We've revised our estimate for official gold sales in 1997 up to 12.1 million ounces (376 tonnes), from 10 million ounces," said Edward Kemp, an analyst with CPM Group in New York.
Estimates for official gold sales in 1996 range from around 200 tonnes to over 550 tonnes, following news mid-January that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of of gold in late 1996.
Gold remained weaker than platinum, as well as silver, Friday, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ending at $7.40 an ounce, up from $6.30 an ounce Thursday and $3.20 on December 31.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $2.10 at $362.50, with NYMEX March palladium, which has been in an uptrend since early December, ending $1.90 higher at $125.50.
